cards.name: OMG BFF LOL
cards.why: You may appreciate its unusual animation, but Tara and Blakey’s shopping, boredom, and emotional fragility are far from your action-adventure staples.

belowFloor.name: Treasure Island

belowFloor.name: Dragon Knight
belowFloor.why: You may enjoy the knight’s dragon-hunting quest for its action-adventure stakes, though its earnest fantasy feels less brisk than your usual favorites.

belowFloor.name: National Treasure: Edge of History

belowFloor.name: Gold

belowFloor.name: Hero Dog: The Journey Home

belowFloor.name: Sweet Tooth

belowFloor.name: The Librarians: The Next Chapter
belowFloor.why: Time travel and magic give you brisk fantasy-adventure fun, though this series is a weaker match for your film-first habits.

belowFloor.name: Property is Theft lol

turns.reply: Here are some those picks for “more of those” — leaning into what you tend to love.
turns.reason: 12 picks ranked for you, from 40 pulled · 12 under your 6.0 bar — shown below

cards.name: The Ones Below
cards.why: A shocking accident turns neighborly tension into domestic dread, offering you a tense psychological thriller without much action or adventure.

cards.name: The Air I Breathe
cards.why: The intersecting crime stories and desperate race to save a loved one bring you intensity, but the brooding drama may weigh against your tastes.

cards.name: Light as a Feather
cards.why: You may enjoy the supernatural death predictions, though this teen-focused series is a bigger format and genre detour.

cards.name: Alex & Me
cards.why: For you, the family-fantasy angle and Alex Morgan’s uplifting pursuit of success offer a lighter change, though little of your usual action.

cards.name: 12 and Holding
cards.why: You may connect with this emotionally charged coming-of-age drama, though its focus on 12-year-olds offers little of your usual action or adventure.

cards.name: Love Finds You In Sugarcreek
cards.why: A stranger’s hidden past brings mystery to an Amish community, but the quiet family-drama tone offers little of your usual action.

cards.name: The Loved Ones
cards.why: Lola’s violent prom-night revenge brings brisk intensity, but the torture-heavy horror may be harsher than your usual action fare.

cards.name: Lucky Them
cards.why: Ellie Klug’s search for a vanished rock star brings a mystery thread, but the wry, low-key music-world drama lacks your usual intensity.

cards.name: Love Finds You in Charm
cards.why: Your taste for adventure is unlikely to find much here: this is a gentle Amish summer romance about friendship and choosing a life.

cards.name: The Client List
cards.why: Riley Parks’ double life gives you family pressure and personal stakes, but this earnest drama series lacks the action and adventure you favor.

cards.name: Outside In
cards.why: You may find the ex-con’s intense small-town bond compelling, but this is relationship-focused drama rather than brisk action or adventure.

cards.name: Certain Women
cards.why: Kelly Reichardt’s quiet stories of rural loneliness move at a contemplative pace that seems far from your preference for brisk intensity.

belowFloor.name: Hounds of Love
belowFloor.why: Vicki’s effort to outwit her abductors brings you taut crime-survival suspense, though the sexual violence and bleak tone are severe.

belowFloor.name: Vicious
belowFloor.why: A cursed box with a deadly rule gives you tense survival stakes, though this leans more horror than action or adventure.

belowFloor.name: Unchosen
belowFloor.why: A young mother’s escape from a sheltered cult and affair with a mysterious stranger offer dark secrets and risk, though it’s a series.

belowFloor.name: Nine Perfect Strangers
belowFloor.why: The resort’s tense group-therapy mystery offers intrigue, but its ensemble series format and measured drama seem less suited to you.

belowFloor.name: Tiny Pretty Things
belowFloor.why: Its tense elite-school betrayal mystery has brisk, cutthroat energy, but the setting and intrigue echo the school-centered thriller you declined.

belowFloor.name: Solos
belowFloor.why: You do revisit science fiction, yet these contemplative isolation stories are a slow anthology series rather than brisk adventure.

belowFloor.name: Extrapolations
belowFloor.why: You get science-fiction and survival stakes across a climate-changing future, but this slow-burn series is a poor match for your film-first habit.

belowFloor.name: Aftersun
belowFloor.why: Your taste for intensity meets Sophie’s troubled memories of her father, but this slow, melancholic drama lacks your usual momentum.

belowFloor.name: Here
belowFloor.why: With its contemplative journey through generations of love and loss, this slow family drama runs against your preference for brisk pacing.

belowFloor.name: Small Things Like These
belowFloor.why: Cillian Murphy’s coal merchant faces a convent’s buried abuse, but the slow, contemplative drama is a poor match for your brisk favorites.

belowFloor.name: Them
belowFloor.why: This bleak anthology about racial terror is a series, and its heavy social drama seems unlike your stronger pull toward films and adventure.

belowFloor.name: I'm Thinking of Ending Things
belowFloor.why: Your thriller interest gets a strange road-trip mystery, though its dreamlike, very slow pace and heavy existential themes may frustrate you.
